question.problem: A student is randomly answering questions in a $10$-question math test. It is known that the student has a $25%$ probability of correctly answering each question. What is the probability that the student answers at most $1$ question correctly? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Let the random variable $X$ be equal to the number of questions that the student answers correctly.

Here, we have the following information:

- there are $n=10$ questions

- the probability of answering each question correctly is $p=25%=0.25$

So, $X$ follows a binomial distribution, where $X∼B(10,0.25).$ 

The number of successes of a binomial random variable has the probability mass function

$$
P(X=x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{n}{x}){p}^{x}(1-p)^{n-x},
$$

where $n$ is the number of experiments, and $p$ is the probability of success on each experiment.

Substituting the above information into the formula for probability mass function, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=x) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{x})(0.25)^{x}(1-0.25)^{10-x} \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{x})(0.25)^{x}(0.75)^{10-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find the probability that the student answers correctly at most $1$ question. So, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 1) & =P(X=0)+P(X=1) \\  & =(0.75)^{10}+(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{10}{1})(0.25)^{1}(0.75)^{10-1} \\  & =(0.75)^{10}+10(0.25)(0.75)^{9} \\  & =0.244\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
